name: Trimless for Gmail V3
tagline: Chrome extension that auto-clicks Gmail's "View entire message" so clipped mail and trimmed quotes open fully expanded.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a single behavior: watch the Gmail DOM, find the trim link or the quoted-text ellipsis, click it. There is no backend, no account, no data, no network effect, and nothing to sync. An agent can produce a working unpacked Manifest V3 content script in one sitting, and a userscript version in less than that. The real cost is not the build, it is that Gmail's markup shifts and your selectors rot, which is roughly what you are paying the vendor to babysit. Also note the paid product is a browser extension, so on Gmail mobile apps neither version does anything at all.
coreLoopDIY: A Manifest V3 content script that watches every opened Gmail thread and automatically clicks the "View entire message" trim link and the quoted-text expand button as soon as they appear.
requirements: Chrome or any Chromium browser with developer mode for loading an unpacked extension
Gmail in the browser, not the mobile app
Willingness to update CSS selectors when Gmail changes its DOM
whatYouLose: Store-signed distribution and auto-updates: you reload an unpacked folder by hand
Someone else fixing the selectors the week Gmail ships a markup change
Firefox and Edge packaging, plus any polish around printing or Gmail's other views
Support, a settings UI, and per-account toggles unless you build them
Nothing on iOS and Android Gmail, same as the paid extension
moatNotes: The moat is maintenance against an unstable DOM, not technology. That is a real service, it is just a small one.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value on offer is not code, it is never thinking about this again. A few dollars to have someone else track Gmail's DOM churn, ship signed updates through the Web Store, and handle the edge cases you would only discover on the one email that mattered is a defensible trade for most people. The DIY build wins if you enjoy owning a fifty-line content script and do not mind fixing it twice a year.
notes: One of the cleanest yes verdicts on the site: a single click, automated, with no server anywhere in the story.
prompt:
Build a Manifest V3 Chrome extension in this empty folder that automatically expands clipped and trimmed Gmail messages.

Stack: plain JavaScript, no build step, no bundler, no npm dependencies. Files only: manifest.json, content.js, options.html, options.js, README.md.

Behavior:
- Content script runs at document_idle on https://mail.google.com/* only.
- Use a single MutationObserver on document.body, debounced to about 150ms, to detect newly rendered message bodies.
- On each pass, find and click Gmail's clipped-message link (the anchor whose href contains "view=lg" or whose text matches "View entire message", case insensitive) and Gmail's quoted-text expander (the element with class containing "ajR" or aria-label matching "Show trimmed content").
- Never click the same element twice: mark handled elements with a data attribute and check it before clicking.
- Guard against loops: cap clicks at 25 per page load and log a warning when the cap is hit.
- Match on multiple selectors with fallbacks, because Gmail obfuscates class names. Put every selector in one SELECTORS object at the top of content.js so it is trivial to patch later.

Options page: two checkboxes stored in chrome.storage.sync, "expand clipped messages" and "expand trimmed quotes", both on by default. Content script reads them before acting.

Explicitly out of scope: any backend, any network request, analytics, telemetry, accounts, licensing, Firefox packaging, Web Store submission.

README must cover: loading the unpacked extension via chrome://extensions with developer mode on, and a short section named "When it breaks" explaining that Gmail changes its DOM and the fix is almost always editing the SELECTORS object.

No secrets and no .env are needed here; if you think you need one, you have misread the task.
